The CFO says 'we try to be under-promising and over-delivering', and Yotta Phase 1 testing was starting at the time of the Q2 call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat its raised plan by 14% and the stock fell 9-11% on the 2027 guide and losses. Q1 2026 (+55% revenue, operating cash flow positive, guide raised) rose about 15%. Q3 2025 record revenue rose about 18% after hours. The revenue beat alone has not decided the sign.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: the street at $51.4-51.9M already sits above the top of the range. If the market expected a large beat, the stock would not be at a 52-week low after a 19% 20-day fall. The residual edge is that the company has beaten its own plan by double digits two quarters running.

findings.finding: On Oct 29 Gorilla signed up to $100M of funding ($111.1M principal, an 11.1% OID) of zero-coupon senior convertibles with Lind Global (13G: 9.99%, 3,065,081 shares). Terms: 1,000,000 pre-delivery shares at $0.001; an alternative conversion at 90% of the 3 lowest VWAPs of 20 days from day 60 or earlier on registration; floor $3.858; 850,612 warrants at $12.8995. The company commits to a resale registration within 30 days and a meeting within 75 days to lift authorized shares from 73.5M to 200M. The money buys advance payments for committed DC capacity and the equity portion of equipment.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell 17.5% on the day the financing became public (2026-10-30), and 26% on the July $125M convertible pricing.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: -17.5% on the day and a drift to $6.59. What the print adds is the Q3 cash balance and the committed capex against it ($228M committed equipment per 247wallst). Any new raise or project-finance shortfall announced on the call would be new. If the market thought funding was settled, the stock would not have kept falling after the -17.5% day.
findings.independence: Lind 13G: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1903145/000092963826004177/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X02/primary_doc.xml ; tickeron description of the -17% day: https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-gorilla-technology-group-grrr-stock-down-17-07-today-24274/. The money funds visible contracted programmes (Batam $2.5B and Yotta), so per the financing rule the use is corroborated. It stays negative because of the terms, not the existence of the raise.

findings.finding: The $125M 7.5% Series B convertible (July) is now registered for resale with up to 22,135,417 underlying shares at 125 shares per $1,000, which implies the conversion price reset from $25.48 to $8.00. That is 80% of the 27,578,506 shares outstanding. The holders are hedge funds (Point72 $23.0M, Graham $21.8M, Moore $11.06M, Hudson Bay, Linden, Highbridge), and a $107M June convertible sits beside it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No release reaction isolates this. The stock fell from $9.46 (Oct 13 close, quoted in the 424B7) to $6.59 since the registration.
findings.why_not_priced: A filed prospectus, not wire copy. Previews quote the July notes at a '$25.48 conversion price, 52% premium'. At $6.59 the $8 reset leaves the notes near the money, so any good print meets convert-holder supply. If this were understood, the rising short interest would read as a hedge rather than as squeeze fuel.
findings.independence: Conversion floor of $8.00 for the July Series B notes from a press-release search snippet (barchart/finviz pricing release); share count also in the Lind 13G arithmetic (3.07M = 9.99%, which implies about 30.7M shares after the pre-delivery shares).

findings.why_not_priced: Public FINRA data. What is unpriced is only the squeeze convexity on a good print. Hedges against near-the-money converts ($8 reset, Lind VWAP notes) do not need covering, so the size is small.

findings.finding: On Oct 9 Gorilla signed a non-binding LOI for its first US data centre (6 MW operating, a path to 36 MW over about 18 months), targeting completion by end of November 2026 with no stated price or funding. On top of $228M of committed equipment, the market read it as another raise and the stock fell 9% on Oct 12. A definitive agreement or its financing is likely on or around this call.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced (-9%). The funding route is undisclosed. If it were settled, the Oct 29 Lind financing would not have been needed for 'advance payments for committed data center capacity'.

findings.finding: Sept 22: Gorilla won a multi-year expansion contract worth 'tens of millions of dollars' with Taiwan's criminal investigation bureau. It includes Nvidia B300 systems, implementation runs Q4 2026 to Q4 2027 plus 3 years of support, and it adds to Q4 and 2027 visibility.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolated. Contract announcements have moved the stock up (June $2.5B deal) but this one is small against the $60-70M Q4 plan.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and undisclosed in size. The stock fell through it. Management said contracts already won are inside guidance (stocktwits, Aug 25), so it likely lands inside the plan: small.

findings.finding: Sept 8: Gorilla said the Yotta programme (more than 25,000 GPUs, India) moved into physical execution, with equipment delivered and being installed. It 'reinforces' the approximately $500M 2027 revenue ambition and flags demand for up to 30,000 GPUs. This is the only post-call statement on the forward guide found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated reaction found; the stock fell through September-October.
findings.why_not_priced: Public release. It matters only as the last management word on 2027; it argues against a cut and does not support a raise to the street's $575M.
findings.independence: Q2 call: Yotta Phase 1 testing starting, Phase 2 equipment 25-30 days out (https://www.webull.com/news/15499649423107072).

findings.finding: On the Q2 call the CFO expected more than $20M of customer collections in September-October and roughly breakeven operating cash flow for FY2026. Q3 cash flow and the September 30 cash balance (against $179.4M at June 30) test that. Eleven weeks later the company took 11%-OID VWAP-priced money, which points to tighter liquidity than the call implied.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026's operating cash flow turning positive coincided with about a +15% reaction. Cash quality has moved this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference only: the Q3 cash figure is not public. Sized small because it is an inference from the timing of the raise, not a document.
findings.independence: Oct 30 6-K financing terms (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001903145/000121390026114094/ea0310294-6k_gorilla.htm). Shares a document with the financing finding, so it is sized small to avoid double count.

lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the Q3 revenue-beat finding cut from +1.5 to +1.0, because the Q2 beat of a raised plan was sold 9-11%.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the Lind financing cut from -1.5 to -1.0. The money funds contracted Batam/Yotta capacity (corroborated); the sign stays negative only for the toxic terms and the authorized-share increase.
Lesson 3 / documents beat inference: the cash-flow-claim finding cut from -0.5 to -0.3, as an inference from the timing of the raise that shares a document with the financing finding.

Lesson 6 (window): the US DC LOI cut from -0.8 to -0.5, since its targeted closing (end-November) falls after the window and only an announcement on the call counts; the closing itself moved to outside_window.

Last lesson (untrustworthy FPI history): already applied in the draft. The base rate was rebuilt from confirmed releases and abs_move_pct left at 13. Lesson 7: short interest checked; kept the positive squeeze finding small because much of the short is convert hedging. p_up and abs_move_pct unchanged.
